January 2013 ## **24****th** **December – 4****th** **January** # Domestic prices edge upwards, activity remains low The domestic market was a little more bullish in the past two weeks, with spot and futures prices for cathode edging upwards. Prior to the 3-day New Year holiday between 1-3 January, we heard that some downstream users were in the market for cathode, fearing that it would be difficult to obtain enough material to keep operating during the holiday. However, this appears to have been limited in volume as SHFE stocks fell only marginally during the period. The SHFE cash copper price rose to RMB57,730/t on 4th January, up from RMB56,610/t at the time of our last publication on 21st December. SHMET spot market prices rose to RMB57,500/t on 4th January, up from RMB56,125/t on 21st December. Arbitrage favourable for imports

The imported cathode market has remained quiet in the past two weeks, as banks offering credit for copper financing were more cautious in issuing the letters of credit needed for trading imported cathode at the end of the year. The spot premium for imported cathode remained unchanged at $40-60/t and the premium for SXEW cathode was also unchanged at $35-45/t. © 2013 CRU International Limited **confidential** January 2013 www.crugroup.com We expect trading volumes in the imported cathode market to swell next week, as more traders return to the market after the New Year’s holiday. We estimate that the stocks we monitor in China fell very marginally to 984,913t by 4th January 2013, from 985,357t two weeks ago. We have not heard of any changes in bonded warehouse stocks over the past two weeks, therefore we keep our estimate of stocks in Shanghai bonded warehouses unchanged at around 750,000-800,000t, and stocks in bonded warehouses in Guangdong at 50,000t. According to data published last week by China '000t Customs,

Chinese imports of semi-finished copper 1,400 and alloy products in the period January-November 1,200 were down by 14.7% y-o-y compared to the same 1,000 period in 2011.  The latest data is part of a continuing 800 trend towards Chinese self-sufficiency in the 600 production of semis.  Imports of semis have almost 400 halved from 2004 levels, and if December continues 200 along the same trajectory, we estimate that 2012 semis 0 imports will be at their lowest levels since 1999. Given the reduction in Chinese imports of semis, during a period when economic growth has been Data: CRU, GTIS **Data: CRU Analysis** *Estimate assuming an annualaverage for Dec largely above 10%, it is noteworthy that the domestic semis industry has been feeling as much competitive pressure as it has. Although picking up slightly in Q4, survey data from the Shanghai Metals Market suggests that operating rates at wirerod producers were between 70-80% for most of 2012, reaching as low as 56% amongst flat-rolled manufacturers and 62% amongst tube manufacturers surveyed. 

The increasing competitive pressure in the sector has been primarily driven by the boom in the manufacturing capacity of low-end semis that can be easily replicated.  This goes some way to explaining why despite the large amounts of over-capacity in the Chinese semis industry, we still saw around 39% of South Korean and 31% of Taiwanese semis products being exported to China in 2012.  Levels of copper flat-rolled product exports, which are typically required to be of higher quality and more exact specifications due to their end-uses in electronics, are even higher with 56% of all South Korean flatrolled products and around 59% of all Taiwanese flat-rolled products being shipped to China.  In our opinion the reduction in imports of semis may start to slow going forward as rising costs in China, a stronger RMB and the higher-end nature of the remaining semis imports reduce China’s competitive edge versus North East Asian semis producers.

China Customs last week also confirmed November imports of cathode at 250,666t, an 8.7% increase on October.  This brings year-to-date imports of cathode to 3.16Mt, a 30.2% increase on the first 11 months of 2011. 

# PMI data signals a stronger year-end 

Chinese economic data for December 2012 was in step with the change in sentiment we have noted in the past month.  The HSBC/Markit China manufacturing PMI furthered its advance into expansionary territory with a reading of 51.5 in December, the strongest since May 2011.  The better reading was driven by improvements in the new orders and purchasing components.  From our conversations with market participants we have heard that semis producers were restocking in the first half of December as order books improved.
